About Rigetti

payload.descriptionPlain:
About the Role
Rigetti Computing is seeking a Director of Quantum System Deployment & Field Engineering to lead the global deployment, integration, commissioning, and lifecycle support of our on-premise quantum computing systems.
In this role, you will build and lead Rigetti's Field Engineering organization, ensuring the successful delivery of complete quantum systems - from factory acceptance through customer installation, commissioning, acceptance, and operational handoff. You will develop the people, processes, and operational standards required to scale commercial deployments worldwide.
Working across Hardware Engineering, Manufacturing, Quantum Engineering, Software, and Program Management, you will ensure every deployed system meets Rigetti's standards for performance, reliability, and customer success.
payload.description:
About the Role

Rigetti Computing is seeking a Director of Quantum System Deployment & Field Engineering to lead the global deployment, integration, commissioning, and lifecycle support of our on-premise quantum computing systems.

In this role, you will build and lead Rigetti's Field Engineering organization, ensuring the successful delivery of complete quantum systems - from factory acceptance through customer installation, commissioning, acceptance, and operational handoff. You will develop the people, processes, and operational standards required to scale commercial deployments worldwide.

Working across Hardware Engineering, Manufacturing, Quantum Engineering, Software, and Program Management, you will ensure every deployed system meets Rigetti's standards for performance, reliability, and customer success.

lists.content:
• Build, lead, and scale Rigetti's global Field Engineering organization.

  • Own the end-to-end deployment of on-premise quantum computing systems, including site readiness, installation, system integration, commissioning, customer acceptance, and operational handoff.

  • Lead deployment of complex systems, including superconducting quantum processors, dilution refrigerators, RF/microwave hardware, control electronics, networking, and supporting infrastructure.

  • Serve as the senior technical escalation point during customer deployments and field operations.

  • Establish deployment processes, field engineering standards, training, documentation, and operational metrics.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Hardware Engineering, Manufacturing, Software, Program Management, and Customer Success to improve deployment readiness, reliability, and customer experience.

  • Drive continuous improvements in deployment efficiency, serviceability, and lifecycle support.

• Master's degree in Physics, Engineering, or a related technical field (Ph.D. preferred).

  • 10+ years of experience deploying, integrating, or supporting complex hardware systems.

  • 3+ years of people management experience.

  • Strong systems engineering background integrating mechanical, electrical, software, networking, and controls systems.

  • Experience with one or more of the following:

  • Quantum computing

  • Cryogenic systems

  • RF/microwave systems

  • Semiconductor equipment

  • Scientific instrumentation

  • Excellent customer-facing leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills.

  • Willingness to travel globally (approximately 30–40%).

• Experience with superconducting quantum computing or dilution refrigerator systems.

  • Experience supporting enterprise, government, or national laboratory customers.

  • Experience building and scaling field engineering organizations.

  • Familiarity with Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), and product lifecycle support.

payload.descriptionPlain:
The Facilities Coordinator is responsible for the day-to-day coordination and execution of facilities operations to ensure a safe, compliant, clean, and efficient work environment across the company's office, laboratory, manufacturing, and support spaces. This role independently manages maintenance requests and vendor relationships, leads small to medium facility projects, and maintains the records, budgets, and metrics that support building systems, compliance, and workplace services. The Facilities Coordinator is a primary point of contact for employees on facilities matters, exercises sound judgment to prioritize competing needs and resolve issues with minimal supervision, and recommends improvements to processes and service delivery.

The Facilities Coordinator partners closely with Facilities leadership, Security, EH&S, IT, Human Resources, Finance, and external service providers to maintain a high-quality workplace.
payload.description:
The Facilities Coordinator is responsible for the day-to-day coordination and execution of facilities operations to ensure a safe, compliant, clean, and efficient work environment across the company's office, laboratory, manufacturing, and support spaces. This role independently manages maintenance requests and vendor relationships, leads small to medium facility projects, and maintains the records, budgets, and metrics that support building systems, compliance, and workplace services. The Facilities Coordinator is a primary point of contact for employees on facilities matters, exercises sound judgment to prioritize competing needs and resolve issues with minimal supervision, and recommends improvements to processes and service delivery.

The Facilities Coordinator partners closely with Facilities leadership, Security, EH&S, IT, Human Resources, Finance, and external service providers to maintain a high-quality workplace.

lists.content:
Facilities Operations

  • Coordinate day-to-day facilities operations across office, laboratory, manufacturing, and support spaces, adjusting priorities as business needs change.

  • Manage intake, prioritization, and tracking of facilities service requests in the work order system, ensuring response and resolution targets are met and escalating issues as appropriate.

  • Plan and schedule preventive and corrective maintenance and track completion against preventive maintenance schedules.

  • Conduct routine facility inspections, identify maintenance and safety needs, and follow issues through to resolution.

  • Monitor building systems, including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, lighting, and fire protection; troubleshoot routine issues and coordinate the response to alarms or system failures.

  • Analyze work order data to identify recurring issues and trends, and recommend corrective actions or process improvements.

  • May provide guidance or on-the-job training to newer team members, interns, or temporary staff.

    • Vendor Management

  • Select, schedule, and manage vendors and contractors for maintenance, repairs, and services, including obtaining and comparing quotes within established guidelines.

  • Ensure vendors and contractors comply with site safety, security, insurance, and permit requirements, including site orientation and escort as needed.

  • Inspect and verify completed work against scope and quality expectations, and resolve deficiencies directly with vendors.

  • Monitor vendor performance and service levels, and maintain vendor contacts, certificates of insurance, contracts, and service history.

    • Projects

  • Lead small to medium facility projects, such as office moves, furniture installations, workspace reconfigurations, and minor improvements, from planning through completion.

  • Develop project schedules, coordinate logistics, and communicate timelines and impacts to affected departments.

  • Track project scope, schedule, and budget; provide status updates and flag risks to Facilities leadership.

  • Support larger capital projects led by Facilities leadership or outside contractors as a project coordinator.

    • Compliance & Safety

  • Support compliance with OSHA, local building codes and regulations, and company policies in partnership with EH&S.

  • Coordinate emergency preparedness activities, such as drills, equipment checks, and inspections.

  • Maintain and audit records for inspections, permits, certifications, and preventive maintenance to keep the site audit-ready.

  • Identify safety concerns, coordinate corrective actions, and follow through to closure.

    • Administrative & Financial Responsibilities

  • Process purchase requests, reconcile invoices, and resolve billing discrepancies with vendors and Finance.

  • Track facilities spend against budget and provide cost data and inputs to Facilities leadership for forecasting.

  • Manage inventories of facilities supplies and equipment, including replenishment.

  • Maintain accurate facility records, floor plans, and maintenance documentation.

  • Develop reports and metrics (for example, work order response times, preventive maintenance completion, and vendor spend) for Facilities leadership.

  • Create and maintain standard operating procedures and process documentation for routine facilities activities.

    • Customer Service

  • Serve as a primary point of contact for employee facilities requests, responding promptly and professionally.

  • Communicate maintenance schedules and planned building activities to affected employees and departments.

  • Follow up to ensure issues are resolved in a timely manner, and handle escalated or sensitive concerns with sound judgment.

Experience

3–5 years of progressively responsible experience in facilities coordination, building operations, property management, or workplace services. Demonstrated experience independently managing vendors and service providers, coordinating projects, and working with work order (CMMS) systems. Experience in laboratory, manufacturing, or other technical environments is a plus.

Required Skills

  • Working knowledge of commercial building systems (HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire/life safety) and ability to troubleshoot routine issues

  • Demonstrated ability to drive solutions to a close

  • Ability to manage multiple competing priorities and exercise sound judgment with minimal supervision

  • Strong project coordination, organizational, and time management skills

  • Experience managing vendors, including scope, quality, and cost

  • Excellent customer service, written, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work across departments

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel in particular) and CMMS/work order software

  • Analytical and problem-solving skills with strong attention to detail

  • Working knowledge of OSHA and building safety compliance requirements

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively

     

    • Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Facilities Management, Business, Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • An Associate's degree with 4+ years of relevant experience, or a high school diploma/GED with 5+ years of relevant experience, will be considered.

•  IFMA FMP, CFM, or comparable facilities management certification. 

  • Demonstrated experience acting as a site facilities lead or primary facilities point of contact, independently resolving complex operational issues with limited management oversight.

  • Experience developing or improving Facilities Operation programs, SOPs, operational standards, vendor management processes, or facilities metrics/KPIs.

  • Experience managing higher-complexity vendor relationships and scopes of work, including evaluating proposals, resolving escalated issues, and identifying opportunities to improve service or cost. 

  • Experience providing technical or operational guidance to less-experienced team members and serving as a resource for facilities best practices.

    • Physical Requirements

  • Ability to walk throughout the facility for extended periods.

  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds and climb ladders or access mechanical areas when necessary.

  • Occasional after-hours support for emergencies or special projects.

    • Success Measures

  • Meet response and resolution targets for facilities requests.

  • Complete preventive and corrective maintenance on schedule and within budget.

  • Manage vendors to scope, safety, quality, and cost expectations.

  • Maintain accurate, audit-ready documentation.

  • Deliver projects on schedule and within budget with minimal disruption to operations.

  • Identify and implement process improvements that increase efficiency, reduce cost, or improve the employee experience.

  • Contribute to a safe, organized, and well-maintained workplace.

payload.descriptionPlain:
About Rigetti
Rigetti Computing is building the world’s most powerful computers to help solve humanity’s most pressing problems. Our quantum computing technology has the potential to transform nearly every industry over the coming decades. As a public company with deep roots in research and engineering, we are expanding our Engineering Operations team to support rapid advances in quantum hardware.
Role Overview
We are seeking an experienced Cryogenics and RF Field Engineer to support Rigetti systems deployed at customer facilities around the world. This is a hands-on, operations-focused role that travels to customer sites globally, working closely with both Rigetti teams and customer stakeholders in a highly collaborative, research-driven environment. The role is not tied to a single site — you'll be deployed to wherever Rigetti systems are installed, with assignments varying in length and location based on program needs.
In this role, you will work closely with physicists, engineers, and technicians to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot advanced RF and cryogenic systems that enable next-generation quantum processors. You will be responsible for ensuring reliable system performance in a production-like environment, including direct ownership of cryogenic infrastructure, RF hardware validation, and rapid debugging of complex, cross-disciplinary issues spanning RF, vacuum, cryogenics, and electronics.
The ideal candidate brings deep laboratory experience with R&D hardware, has worked in customer-facing or field-deployed environments, is comfortable with international travel and working across time zones and cultures, and has direct hands-on experience operating and debugging dilution refrigerators.

lists.content:
• Test, validate, and debug custom RF control systems using advanced electronic test equipment such as network analyzers, oscilloscopes, DMMs, and internally developed tools

  • Operate, monitor, and debug dilution refrigerators, including cooldowns, steady-state operation, and fault diagnosis

  • Operate, troubleshoot and service cryogenic and vacuum systems, including scroll pumps, turbo pumps, cryo compressors, high-vacuum components, and cold traps

  • Perform helium leak detection, pump rebuilds, and thermal system management

  • Assemble, validate, and install complex electro-mechanical, cryogenic, vacuum, and RF assemblies with exceptional attention to detail

  • Contribute to test plan development and execute validation testing for next-generation RF hardware

  • Participate in an on-call rotation to support system uptime in a customer-facing environment, potentially spanning multiple time zones

  • Prepare, inspect, and package quantum chip assemblies for testing

  • Follow established procedures and contribute to the creation and improvement of standard operating procedures and best practices

  • Read and interpret CAD drawings, schematics, and engineering specifications

  • Work directly with customer teams across different regions to support system operation, issue resolution, and ongoing optimization

  • Navigate logistics of international travel, including customs/import considerations for tools and equipment, visas, and site-specific access requirements

  • 35+% travel required, including international travel to customer sites; frequency and destinations will vary by program

• Technical background in Physics, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent industrial experience (MS or PhD a plus)

  • Strong proficiency with general-purpose electronic test equipment (oscilloscopes, network analyzers, multimeters, DC power supplies, etc.)

  • Direct, hands-on experience operating and troubleshooting dilution refrigerators (required)

  • Substantial hands-on experience working with sub-Kelvin cryogenic systems

  • Experience operating and maintaining high-availability laboratory or industrial equipment

  • Experience assembling, servicing, and maintaining scientific instruments or complex electro-mechanical systems

  • Familiarity with vacuum systems, vacuum plumbing, P&IDs, and standard fittings and practices; strong experience in vacuum equipment assembly and debug using helium leak detection

  • Working knowledge of statistical methods for test and validation (e.g., DOE, Six Sigma, simulation)

  • Attention to detail in documentation (writing and following Work Instructions and Standard Operating Procedures) plus excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Experience working with external vendors, partners, or customers across different regions and cultural contexts

  • Willingness and ability to travel internationally on short notice, and to hold or obtain necessary travel documentation (passport, visas)

• Experience in field deployment or on-site support roles at customer or partner facilities, particularly in international settings

  • Familiarity with import/export logistics for scientific or electronic equipment

  • Programming or scripting experience in Python or related languages

  • Additional language proficiency relevant to target deployment regions
